$comment: The deployable services and the order they are deployed in (docs/architecture/16 §1, §4).
One catalogue rather than a railway.json per service. Railway's config-as-code is read
when Railway builds from the repository; these services run images CI built, scanned and
pushed, so a railway.json sitting here would be a file nothing reads — and this codebase
has found that bug four times already. infra/scripts/railway-deploy.ts applies these
settings through the Railway API instead, which is a thing that happens rather than a
`phase` is the deployment order from doc 16 §4 and is not cosmetic: workers are deployed
before the API so new consumers exist before new events do, and the web applications last
because they are the only ones a person is looking at while it happens.
`environments` restricts a service to the environments that should run it. Absent means every environment, which is what all but the seed want.

`region` is applied to every service instance. It was prose in the README for a release — `Production runs in EU West (Amsterdam)` — and prose is not a setting: the first project stood up under this pipeline landed in US West, because nothing here ever said otherwise to Railway. Decision D-01 option A and the EU data-residency commitment in docs/architecture/19 are the reason it is this value.

`ams`, not `europe-west4`. Both name Amsterdam and the Google-style one is Railway's legacy spelling, but Railway's own tooling reads the legacy name as a *different* region and plans a destructive move of any attached volume to reach it. None of the services below carries a volume, so the blast radius here is nil — but the managed Postgres does, and somebody copying a region out of this file onto a database is the likeliest way that mistake gets made.

image.$comment: One repository, one tag per commit, one image per Dockerfile target: ghcr.io/<repo>/<target>:sha-<commit>.

services.name: migrate
services.$comment: Runs to completion before anything else starts. Expand-only (doc 16 §4), as app_owner.

services.name: seed
services.$comment: Preview only. A production environment that seeded itself would invent two tenants nobody asked for; a preview that did not would be an empty service desk nobody can click on. `node dist/seed.js` and not `pnpm seed`: it runs in the migration image, which carries no package manager.

services.name: admin
services.$comment: One replica: the console is used by a handful of people and a second instance buys nothing but a second thing to roll back.

managed.$comment: Provisioned once from Railway's own catalogue rather than deployed by this pipeline. Listed so the layout is complete and nobody concludes they were forgotten.
